lines: I did. Still breathing, still standing. That counts for more than it sounds.
Back to the village in one piece. I will remember who helped make that true.
I am here, breathing, and trying not to <shake>shake</shake>. That is enough for now.
I found a really good hiding place, but I cannot tell you or it stops being good.
The bell is loud up close. I learned that by mistake.
Today I found a place where grown-ups forget to look down.
<jump>Hi again!</jump>
Hi! I remember your face a little.
Hello again! I was practicing saying hello first.
I can say hello from here.
Hello from this safe distance.
I can <wavy>wave</wavy> from here. That counts.
A question? I know three things: doors, bells, and which path has puddles.
Ask a grown-up. They like sounding certain.
I know where the puddles are and which door creaks loudest.
Once I ran all the way around the well and did not fall in. That is the whole story, but it was <jump>very exciting</jump>.
I had a <wavy>dream</wavy> I was tall enough to see over every fence.
I counted every door on this side of the square. Then I forgot the number and had to start over.
Why did the bell ring? Because it had something <jump>important</jump> to say!
If I stand very still, chores cannot see me.
Why did the door close? Because the wind was bossy.
